head_commit.message:
test: concentrate secret-hygiene assertions in fixture snapshots

Add per-role secret snapshots to the exchange fixture: taken while a
core's persistent secrets are live, they capture backing-array aliases
and, after a terminal operation, assert the core dropped its references
and the arrays were zeroed. The snapshots are now the only test-surface
code that knows the cores' field layout; the 22 state.core reach-ins
across eight hygiene tests are gone.

The responder snapshot tracks all five transcript byte fields rather
than only the concatenation, so a clear() that skips the transcript
wipe now fails TestSessionISKSurvivesCoreClear (verified by mutation).

CONTEXT.md: add the Secret snapshot term and name it in the Exchange
fixture entry.

Signed-off-by: Joshua Sargent <the-sarge@the-sarge.com>

head_commit.message:
docs: correct scalar-sampling analysis and review-packet accuracy

Pre-outreach dry-run review fixes, all documentation/comment-only:

- The claimed ~2^-125 canonical-decode rejection window [L, 2^252) is
  empty: masking bounds every sample below 2^252 < L, so the branch is
  unreachable defense-in-depth. Corrected in security-assessment,
  spec-matrix, and the crypto.go comment; dated correction note added
  to security-spec-audit.
- Reconciled the four divergent scalar-sampling descriptions (handoff
  'zero retry', project-plan, spec-matrix, assessment) to one story.
- Documented that LocalAssociatedData mismatches do not fail the
  exchange (probe-verified): confirmation binds transmitted ADa/ADb,
  so outer commitments in AD require a PeerAssociatedData check;
  automatic fail-closed values belong in Context/SessionID.
- Dropped session ID from the threat model's CI enumeration (sid is
  bound separately into generator string, ISK, and confirmation tags).
- Replaced the stale TestMessageParserFieldSizeLimits reference with
  the real framing catalogue tests.
- Bumped the handoff date and stated which ref reviewers read and why
  the pinned f7efa6a evidence applies at main.

No behavior, public API, or dependency change.

Signed-off-by: Joshua Sargent <the-sarge@the-sarge.com>
